completions.completed_label: Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia Type 2 (MEN2) with medullary thyroid carcinoma and pheochromocytoma
completions.reason: The patient presents with symptoms and lab findings consistent with both medullary thyroid carcinoma (neck swelling, elevated calcitonin) and pheochromocytoma (palpitations, sweating, elevated metanephrines), which are key components of MEN2.
support_spans: A 31-year-old woman presented with a 7-year history of episodic palpitations, profuse sweating, and severe headaches.
Over the same period, she noted a gradually enlarging anterior neck swelling without compressive symptoms or signs of thyroid dysfunction.
24-hour urinary metanephrines >10 000 µg (normal 25–312 µg) and normetanephrines 8791 µg (normal <600 µg)
